newsitem.title: USA: National Semi seen transforming itself.
newsitem.headline: National Semi seen transforming itself.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp chief executive Brian Halla seems to have found the formula that is finally reviving the sluggish chip maker.
National not only beat expectations in posting a $0.21 a share profit for the second quarter, it also surprised analysts with its very strong orders and lean inventory.
And, when new products started under Halla go to market next year, the company could become a growth stock, analysts say.
"The whole character of this company looks like it might change," said Cowen & Co analyst Drew Peck.
Peck described the change as being from a company "mired in mediocrity" to one that's "a higher than average grower."
Prudential Securities analyst Mark Edelstone agreed.
"The foundation is in place for a more profitable, less cyclical and stronger company," he added.
And Jon Joseph of Montgomery Securities called National Semiconductor "our favorite large-cap turnaround play" on which it has a strong buy recommendation.
All three expressed surprised that National's problems with high inventories were over and that orders were 110 percent of sales for the quarter.
"The company is showing improvement faster than I would have guessed and the most interesting aspect is it is happening even before we see the impact of a rebuilt product portfolio," Peck said.

National, like most of the semiconductor industry, was saddled with bloated inventories inhouse and among customers most of this year. The $0.21 for the quarter compares with year ago earnings of $0.57 a share, but exceeds Wall Street's mean estimate of $0.18 a share tallied by First Call.
Edelstone said the key issue for National was getting rid of inventory. Having done so, it could build up orders.
